# Compost pile

## The setup

Three bays made from six pallets that Colin Prowse brought back from the builders' merchant in Chudleigh in March 2023, wired together with fencing staples. Each bay about 1 m square and 1 m high. Old carpet over the top, which the purists frown upon, but it keeps the heat in and the rain off.

- Bay A: filling
- Bay B: cooking
- Bay C: finished, or near enough

Rat mesh (13 mm galvanised, 5 m roll, £23.90) stapled under bays A and B after the trouble in autumn 2023.

## Greens and browns

I don't weigh, I count buckets. Roughly two buckets of brown to one of green.

Greens: grass clippings (thin layers only, or it slimes), veg trimmings and tea leaves from the house, comfrey, nettle tops before they seed, coffee grounds from the Old Inn which Sally saves for me in a catering tub.

Browns: shredded cardboard, egg boxes, straw from Tom Hext's barn, autumn leaves (but most leaves go to the leaf cage), hedge prunings put through the shredder.

Spent kombucha mats from Clare's batch go in too, see [[Kombucha SCOBY]]; they vanish in a week.

## Temperatures

Long-stemmed thermometer, 50 cm probe, bought at the Devon County Show 2023 for £18.

- 2024-06-11: 63°C in the middle of bay B, three days after filling with a full load of grass and straw
- 2024-06-20: 48°C
- 2024-07-02: 31°C, turned it into bay C, back up to 52°C two days later
- 2024-10-14: 22°C, no matter what I do once the nights cool

Anything over 55°C for a few days should finish off most weed seeds. I don't trust it to do blight, so blighted tomato and potato tops go to the council bin instead (see [[Tomato blight]]).

## Turning

Every two to three weeks in summer, once a month in winter if at all. My back says once a month in summer too. A long-handled fork with a D handle, not the spade.

## What not to put in

- Bindweed and couch roots (they go in a water barrel to drown for six weeks first)
- Blight
- Cooked food (rats)
- Cat litter, obviously, though a neighbour once asked
- Glossy paper

## How long it takes

From starting bay B to usable in bay C: about 4 months in summer, 8 months over winter. The 2023 summer batch was ready by November and went on the [[Raised bed soil mix]] top-up in February 2024. Sieve it through a 12 mm riddle and whatever won't go through goes back into bay A as a starter.

## Mistakes, in no order

1. Too much grass in one go, May 2023. Stinking slimy layer. Forked in cardboard to fix.
2. Too dry in August 2024. Ran a hose on it for ten minutes, temperature back up next day.
3. Left the carpet off in the January 2024 storms; the whole bay was sodden and cold for a month.
4. Put avocado stones in. They are still there.
